theme: 3 terms on patterns in switch: matching several values at once, naming part of a match, and the operator behind every case

terms.definition: A pattern that matches several values at once by listing them in parentheses.
terms.example: Use a Tuple Pattern to check the status code and the message together.

terms.definition: A pattern that matches a value and also gives part of it a new name with `let` or `var`.
terms.example: A Value-Binding Pattern pulls the width out, so we can print it.

terms.definition: The `~=` operator that checks whether a value fits a pattern, which every `case` uses behind the scenes.
terms.example: The Pattern Matching Operator is why a range works in a `case`.

video.description:
Learn to explain pattern matching in Swift: Tuple Pattern, Value-Binding Pattern & Pattern Matching Operator, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Tuple Pattern - A pattern that matches several values at once by listing them in parentheses.
Value-Binding Pattern - A pattern that matches a value and also gives part of it a new name with `let` or `var`.
Pattern Matching Operator - The `~=` operator that checks whether a value fits a pattern, which every `case` uses behind the scenes.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Tuple Pattern, Value-Binding Pattern & ~= Operator | Day 48
landscape.description:
Explain Tuple Pattern, Value-Binding Pattern & Pattern Matching Operator in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
튜플 패턴, 값 바인딩 패턴, 패턴 매칭 연산자 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Tuple Pattern - A pattern that matches several values at once by listing them in parentheses.
한국어: 튜플 패턴: 괄호 안에 나열해서 여러 값을 한 번에 맞춰 보는 패턴

Value-Binding Pattern - A pattern that matches a value and also gives part of it a new name with `let` or `var`.
한국어: 값 바인딩 패턴: 값을 맞춰 보면서 그 일부에 let이나 var로 새 이름을 붙이는 패턴

Pattern Matching Operator - The `~=` operator that checks whether a value fits a pattern, which every `case` uses behind the scenes.
한국어: 패턴 매칭 연산자: 값이 패턴에 맞는지 확인하는 ~= 연산자로, 모든 case가 내부에서 사용함

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why each case has parentheses, how to name part of a match and how a range matches one number, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these switch patterns in English?

dialogue.title: Why the parentheses?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, why does each `case` in this `switch` have parentheses?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because `response` is a tuple. Each case is a Tuple Pattern.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. The underscore means we don't care about that part.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a Value-Binding Pattern. It catches the message and names it `text`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait, how can `400..<500` match one number?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swift uses the Pattern Matching Operator. It checks if 404 is in the range.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I use the Pattern Matching Operator myself?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure, in an `if`. But a Tuple Pattern with a Value-Binding Pattern usually reads better.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Tuple Pattern for pairs, Value-Binding Pattern for names, Pattern Matching Operator for ranges.
A Tuple Pattern checks two values in one case.
